title: Likelihood-Ratio Calibration for Monotone Dose Curves under Unknown Flatness
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4; math and rubric pass, but the only quantified calibration design requires about 10^29 unexecuted primitive evaluations and supplies no executed certified critical value.
gap_reasons: The only quantified calibration design requires about 10^29 unexecuted primitive evaluations, and the package supplies no executed certified critical value or evidence of useful conservatism.

The proposed replacement of existing calibration therefore remains a computational possibility, leaving a specialized certification contribution whose demonstrated inferential usefulness falls below the field floor and limits the projected paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery assembled all-threshold continuum-flatness canonical LR certification, uniform localization down to positive exponents approaching zero, a boundary-corrected exact evaluator and a fixed-B polynomial work bound. The calibration scope was broadened to the full accessible Doss v1 theorem class, and eight cited leaves were source-attested with an explicit proof bridge for independence under rescaling. Math and rubric passed, but the only quantified design needs about 1.058e29 unexecuted evaluations; no practical certified critical value was delivered, so the final novelty tier is incremental and formalization was not entered.
tldr: The canonical likelihood-ratio law for a monotone G-computed dose curve depends on its unknown positive finite flatness. For each fixed finite \(B\), the envelope \(H_B\) over every \(0<\beta\le B\) has an all-threshold numerical probability certificate with arbitrarily reducible horizontal and vertical error. Coefficient-invariant Brownian barriers and a boundary-corrected dual area permit positive flatness grids, fair-bit simulation and exact outward arithmetic. Independent simulation and positive continuous threshold jitter give pointwise statistical coverage for the same non-split LR statistic on the full accessible Doss v1 Theorem 3.5 class, and causal coverage when source Assumption I is supplied. A predetermined finite terminal family permits capped adaptive refinement with a coarse work bound; useful adaptive savings are not established.
gap: Doss v1 establishes a fixed-flatness LR law and motivates unknown-flatness calibration through simulated ordering. Generic Brownian simulation does not certify \(H_B\) over a continuous flatness interval approaching zero, including its whole-line, discretization and arithmetic errors.
fill: The new mathematical step is a common switching-slope and spatial barrier after coefficient renormalization, assembled with a boundary-corrected conjugate energy and a complete numerical probability ledger. The resulting theorem targets the same non-split pointwise causal profile used for nurse staffing.
